DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Hospital Information
Hospital Name: CityCare Multispecialty Hospital
Hospital Registration No: HOSP/AP/556677 (NABH Accredited)
Address: Plot No. 45, Jubilee Hills, Hyderabad – 500033
Contact: +91-40-44556677
Patient & Insurance Details
Patient Name: Ramesh Kumar
Age / Gender: 45 Years / Male
UHID: HSP-556677
Government ID: Aadhaar (XXXX-XXXX-1234)
Health Policy Number: POL-12345678
Claim ID / Reference No: CLM-2024-001
Insurance Company: Medicare Ltd
TPA Name: HealthAssist TPA
Hospitalization Details
Date & Time of Admission: 12-03-2024 at 10:45 AM
Date & Time of Discharge: 17-03-2024 at 04:30 PM
Total Length of Stay: 5 Days
Ward / Room Category: General Ward
Bed Number: GW-12
Chief Complaints at Admission
(cid:127) High-grade fever for 3 days
(cid:127) Severe body aches and headache
(cid:127) Nausea and multiple episodes of vomiting
(cid:127) Generalized weakness and reduced oral intake
Clinical History
The patient was apparently well three days prior to admission when he developed sudden onset high-grade fever
associated with chills, myalgia, retro-orbital pain, and vomiting. There was no history of bleeding manifestations,
breathlessness, chest pain, or altered sensorium. No significant past medical history of diabetes, hypertension,
cardiac illness, or previous similar episodes was reported.
Examination Findings on Admission
General Condition: Moderately ill, conscious, oriented to time, place, and person.
Pulse Rate: 96/min, regular
Blood Pressure: 110/70 mmHg
Temperature: 102°F
Respiratory Rate: 18/min
Systemic Examination: Cardiovascular, respiratory, and central nervous systems were clinically normal. Mild
hepatomegaly was noted on abdominal examination.
Investigations
(cid:127) Complete Blood Count (CBC)
(cid:127) Dengue NS1 Antigen Test (Positive)
(cid:127) Liver Function Tests (SGOT & SGPT elevated)
(cid:127) Renal Function Tests (Within normal limits)
Diagnosis
Provisional Diagnosis: Viral Fever
Final Diagnosis: Dengue Fever (NS1 Positive) with Mild Thrombocytopenia
Treatment & Hospital Course
The patient was managed conservatively with intravenous fluids, antipyretics, anti-emetics, and close monitoring of
platelet counts and vital parameters. Platelet counts were monitored daily and showed gradual improvement. No
platelet transfusion was required during the hospital stay. The patient remained hemodynamically stable throughout
the hospitalization and showed symptomatic improvement.
Condition at Discharge
The patient was afebrile, clinically stable, and tolerating oral diet well. Vital signs were within normal limits. There
were no active complaints at the time of discharge.
Medications at Discharge
(cid:127) Tablet Paracetamol 650 mg – One tablet orally every 6 hours as needed for fever
(cid:127) Oral Rehydration Solution (ORS) – As advised
Discharge Advice
(cid:127) Adequate oral fluid intake
(cid:127) Avoid strenuous physical activity for one week
(cid:127) Monitor for warning signs such as bleeding, persistent vomiting, or abdominal pain
(cid:127) Follow up with CBC after 7 days or earlier if symptoms worsen
Follow-up
Follow-up consultation scheduled after 7 days with treating physician along with repeat blood investigations.
Treating Doctor
Dr. Anil Sharma
MD (General Medicine)
Medical Registration No: AP/MD/334455
Authorized Signatory & Hospital Seal
